newsitem.title: USA: BackWeb to buy Lanacom in push technology merger.
newsitem.headline: BackWeb to buy Lanacom in push technology merger.

text.p: BackWeb Technologies said it has agreed to buy Lanacom Inc, and would incorporate its software into BackWeb's family of push products for delivering applications and information within companies.

The privately-held companies did not disclose terms of the deal, which they expect to close in mid-July. BackWeb executives said they expect to retain a majority of Lanacom's 24 employees and to integrate its products within four months.
Tony Davis, president and CEO of Lanacom, based in Toronto, will become vice president for product development at BackWeb, including responsibility for research and development.

The deal is the latest sign of consolidation in the emerging market for so-called push technologies, which enable content such as software updates and news to be delivered automatically to computer users using networks like the Web.

"We think we just acquired the company which has the best tools in the market for building, extracting, combining and manipulating information," BackWeb CEO Eli Barkat said in an interview, adding users can in minutes use Lanacom's tools to build their own customized automated update services.
Such tools can be used to extract updating information on a company's rivals, for example, or to provide notification when airline ticket prices drop to below a certain level.
Barkat said the companies had been talking for some time and had gotten down to serious discussions in the last two months which culminated in the merger.

"We're a privately held company and so our strategy is not to grow by acquisition," he added. "But the thing about this company is it's very rare that you run into a company that builds such a complimentary technology that works so well on top of what you do (as Lanacom)."

Phil Heye, director of product management at BackWeb, said the two companies' client software -- used on desktop computers -- will be integrated together and Lanacom's Headliner server software will be offered as an optional add-on module.
Lanacom has between half a dozen and a dozen "fairly well committed" customers, he said. This includes one customer which has already integrated the two companies' products together.
BackWeb said it will maintain Lanacom's Toronto offices as a development site.
BackWeb added that the integrated products will support both Microsoft Corp's Channel Definition Format (CDF) push delivery protocol and Netscape Communications Corp's Netcaster push delivery system.

Both companies also have agreements with Tibco Software Inc and Barkat said the combined company will provide a server option prividing real-time multicast push technologies using Tibco's multicast technology, which enables content to be sent out to multiple locations at the same time.
Tibco is a subsidiary of Reuters Holdings Plc and Cisco Systems Inc recently made a minority investment in Tibco Software Inc.
